details_json.description:
JSON string as written (actor/action/repo-shaped data only — never
IP, user-agent, or token material).

AuditListResponse.description:
A page of the audit log.

Pagination: request `?limit=<1..=200>` (default 50) and optionally
`?cursor=before:<id>` — the `next_cursor` value of the previous page.
Rows come newest-first (descending; id order matches ts order because
ids are assigned at insert). Follow `next_cursor` until `has_more` is
false.

next_cursor.description: `before:<id>` of this page's oldest row, or null when exhausted.

BatchGetRequest.description: Request body of the batch fetch.

BatchGetResponse.description:
Batch fetch result. Membership-enforced: an id without a
`repo_blobs(repo, id)` row lands in `missing` even when the CAS holds
the file (cross-repo isolation). A missing or unreadable file after a
membership hit is also reported in `missing` (logged server-side).

BatchPutEntry.description: One entry of the batch PUT.

data_b64.description:
Standard (padded) base64 of the payload — single line, no
whitespace; large payloads should use the raw PUT instead.

id.description: 64 lowercase hex id that must equal `BLAKE3(decoded data)`.

BatchPutRequest.description: Request body of the batch PUT.

cs.description:
64-hex id of the changeset whose edit introduced the line
(first-parent semantics: compared against the first parent).

text.description: Line text without its trailing newline.

BlameResponse.description:
A blame of one file at one changeset. Pinned shape:
`{at, path, binary, binary_code, degraded, poisoned_cs, lines}` —
`binary: true` carries the stable code `blame_binary` in
`binary_code` and empty lines (HTTP 200: a binary file is a valid,
structured empty blame, not an error); an empty file blames as empty
`lines` with `binary: false`.

binary.description: True when the file at `at` is not valid UTF-8: blame does not run.

degraded.description:
Part of the walked chain could not be resolved exactly: a quarantined
node, or the walk reaching a row-less ancestor of root (the
root-boundary leg — degraded without any quarantine). Lines below
the boundary are attributed to the boundary changeset itself (named
in `poisoned_cs`) — attribution bounded below by the boundary,
never silently presented as exact.

poisoned_cs.description:
The changesets the read degraded at: quarantined nodes on the walked
chain, or the boundary node of the root leg (64-hex ids).

ChangesetChange.description: One change of a create request.

blob.description: 64 lowercase hex blob id; required for add/mod, forbidden for del.

exec.description: Exec bit; required for add/mod, forbidden for del.

size.description: Content byte length; required for add/mod, forbidden for del.

ChangesetChangeOut.description: One change of a changeset fetch response.

blob.description: Hex blob id; null for deletes.

ChangesetRootResponse.description: The root-tree pointer of a changeset.

changes.description:
The file changes, sorted by path bytes — the server rejects
unsorted input, it never re-sorts (the id is the client's
responsibility).

parents.description:
Parent changeset ids; the public API takes at most one (imports
create 2-parent changesets through the db layer, not this route).

timestamp_ns.description: Author timestamp in ns; omitted → the server clock.

CreateRefRequest.description: Request body of the ref move.

oneOf.description:
`null` = create the ref (409 `ref_conflict` if it exists);
`{"version": v}` = move only while the current version is `v`.

CreateSnapshotRequest.description:
Request body of snapshot create. `trees` carries the canonical bytes of
the referenced tree and every subtree below it (standard base64): the
client builds them bottom-up, and the server writes their rows inside the
create transaction so the blob-presence walk can traverse them.

tree_id.description: The root tree id, 64 lowercase hex; must be among `trees`.

trees.description: Canonical tree bytes (root + full subtree closure), base64.

ttl_secs.description:
TTL in seconds (default 604800 = 7d; below 60 or above 31622400 =
366 days → 422. The ceiling is a server-side safety bound; the plan
pins only the 1-minute floor).

principal.description: Principal name; created (or re-roled to `role`) if absent.

scope_path.description:
Segment-aligned path scope (`None`/null = whole repo). Stored
without a trailing slash; a trailing slash is rejected (422).

ttl_days.description: Token lifetime in days; null = never expires.

a_blob.description: Hex blob id on the `a` side; null for adds.

b_blob.description: Hex blob id on the `b` side; null for deletes.

DiffResponse.description: A path-level diff between two changesets' root trees, sorted by path.

ErrorCode.description: The closed error-code registry: every value `error.code` may take. Each code's pinned HTTP status and recovery `details` are documented in the README error-code table.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The envelope every error response uses.

details.description: Structured recovery data; recoverable codes carry it (e.g. `ref_conflict` carries the current ref version, land conflicts carry the resolution recipe).

base.description:
Advisory base hint: ignored for the rebase (the server always
rebases onto head's merge-base with main); when present and not
head's parent, the response carries a note.

head.description: Head changeset id (64 lowercase hex) to land onto `main`.

key.description:
Idempotency key, scoped to (repo, principal). A settled key with the
same head replays its recorded result; with a different head → 409
`idempotency_key_settled`. After a conflict (which leaves the key
unsettled) the same key re-lands. While a land with this key is in
flight, a concurrent request joins it (see the module doc).

landed.description:
The changeset main points at after the land (the rebased head when
the chain was rewritten).

main.description: The `main` ref target after the land (== `landed`).

note.description: Present when the advisory `base` was not head's parent.

rebased.description: How many changesets were rebased (rewritten with new ids).

LandStatusResponse.description: Response of the land status read.

head.description: The head the key was landed with.

state.description: `done` (a committed pending row is unobservable — single writer).

LandStatusResult.description: The recorded result of a settled land.

LogResponse.description:
A `/log` page: the first-parent chain, newest first. The chain itself is
the deterministic order.

next_cursor.description: `after:<id>` of this page's last entry, or null when done.

merge_base.description:
Hex id of the best common ancestor, or null when the two changesets
share no history.

PathLogResponse.description:
A `?path=` page: the log-page shape plus the derived-read contract
fields. `degraded` with a non-empty `poisoned_cs` says part of the
index was quarantined — the page may be missing touches of those
changesets (never presented as complete history).

degraded.description:
True when a quarantined node's primary file changes touch this
path (listed in `poisoned_cs`) — exactly the touches the derived
index may be missing. A path no quarantined node touched is never
flagged.

next_cursor.description: `after:<id>` of this page's last entry, or null when done.

poisoned_cs.description:
The quarantined changesets whose touches may be missing from this
page (64-hex ids).

PresentRequest.description: Request body of the presence check.

PresentResponse.description:
Presence-check result: ids whose object file is absent from the CAS.
Membership is NOT consulted — `present` answers "is the content on
disk", not "may this repo read it".

RefResponse.description: A ref read or move result.

target.description: Lowercase-hex target id, or null for an unborn ref.

version.description: Monotonic version — supply as `expected.version` on move (CAS).

RejectedEntry.description:
A batch-PUT rejection: the entry id and its error code (`malformed` for
hex/base64/hash mismatches, `too_large` over the 64 MiB cap).

RepoListResponse.description:
A page of the repo list.

Pagination: request `?limit=<1..=200>` (default 50) and optionally
`?cursor=after:<id>` — the `next_cursor` value of the previous page,
i.e. `after:<id>` where `<id>` is the last repo id of that page. Follow
`next_cursor` until `has_more` is false.

next_cursor.description: `after:<id>` of this page's last repo, or null when done.

bytes.description: Sum of uncompressed sizes over this repo's objects.

cbytes.description: Sum of on-disk (compressed) sizes over this repo's objects.

objects.description: Objects referenced by this repo via `repo_blobs`.

RepoSummary.description: One repo in a listing page.

SnapshotBlobStored.description: The id echo of a successful snapshot-blob PUT.

SnapshotCreated.description:
Created snapshot body (201 + `Location`; an identical re-POST → 200
carrying the RECORDED expiry from the snapshot row, never a recomputed
one).

StoredObject.description: One stored object in a batch fetch.

StoredObjectId.description: The object id echo of a successful PUT.

TokenCreated.description: Created token body. `token` is printed exactly once — save it.

expires_ns.description: Absolute expiry in ns since the epoch, or null (never).

TokenSummary.description:
A listed token (revoked tokens drop out of the list; the audit log
records revocations).

TreeEntryOut.description: One entry of a tree listing.

object_id.description: Blob id for files, child tree id for dirs.

size.description: File: content bytes. Dir: recursive total.

VersionResponse.description: Version response body: server name, crate version, wire protocol version.

scope_path.description: Segment-aligned path scope, or null (whole repo).

info.description:
naatre VCS server API.

Conventions: every error uses the envelope `{error: {code, message, retryable, details, request_id}}` with codes from the closed registry; creates return 201 + Location; a re-PUT of an existing blob is an idempotent 200; a busy single writer answers 503 + Retry-After with `retryable: true`.

Pagination: `/v1/repos` pages ascend with `cursor=after:<id>`; `/v1/audit` pages descend with `cursor=before:<id>`. `next_cursor` of a page feeds the next request until `has_more` is false.

get.description:
Read-during-backlog: any chain node still queued or deriving → 503
`derivation_pending` + `Retry-After` (never an empty-as-if-no-history
answer). Quarantine degrades, never lies: the walk stops at the
quarantined node and every unresolvable line is attributed to it (its
blob provably contains those lines), with `degraded: true` and the node
in `poisoned_cs`.

get.summary:
Blames one file at one changeset (any authenticated principal) by

at each node that touched the path, the line diff between its blob and
the parent's blob attributes the introduced lines. First touched node
with no parent blob = the add; the walk stops there.

get.description:
Acceleration contract: when both endpoints' commit_graph rows are done
and untainted, the walk runs on the derived skip lists
(`merge_base_skip`); anything else — kind unregistered, a pending,
quarantined, or tainted endpoint, undecodable output — falls back to
the plain generation-bounded walk. Merge-base never answers 503
`derivation_pending`: the fallback walk is exact and cheap, so pending
derivation costs only the acceleration, not the read (a quarantined or
tainted node degrades it the same way).

post.description:
Rules: `main` is rejected with 422 (`main` moves only via land, M4);
`target` must be 64 lowercase hex (else 400); `expected: null` creates
the ref (409 `ref_conflict` if it exists); `expected: {"version": v}`
moves only while the current version is `v` (stale → 409
`ref_conflict` with `current_version`/`current_target` details). A move
must also be a fast-forward: the new target has to contain the current
one (merge-base(current, new) == current), else 422 `not_fast_forward`
— a target that is not a changeset of this repo cannot prove
containment and is refused identically.

Creates a snapshot (writer and above, path-scope enforced over the
closure's file paths): validates the posted tree closure, writes the
tree rows, checks every referenced blob is present under

transaction. A missing blob rejects the whole POST with 422 and a capped
`details.missing_blobs` list, zero rows written. An identical re-POST
answers 200 with the RECORDED expiry; a differing `ttl_secs` is 422 with
that expiry in `details`; re-POSTing an expired id is 410.
